response.text: Accrual and cash-basis are two ways to record money coming in and going out. With cash basis, you record income only when you actually get paid and expenses only when you pay them — it’s simple and shows your bank cash flow. With accrual accounting, you record income when you earn it (for example, when you deliver a product or finish a service) and record expenses when you incur them (when you receive goods or services), even if money changes hands later. So, if you do work in December but are paid in January, accrual shows the income in December; cash basis shows it in January. Accrual gives a clearer picture of how the business is doing over time; cash basis is easier to keep and focused on actual cash on hand.
